Subject: Production: sudden 5xx/429 surge impacting inference - need immediate help

Hey Neha,

We're seeing a huge spike in 5xx and 429 responses across our production routes hitting Redwood's hosted endpoint since ~07:45 PST. Latency has jumped from ~120ms p50 to 2.3s p95, and several of our upstream workers are retrying aggressively which looks like a retry storm. Our autoscaling shows pools rapidly hitting GPU capacity and the Hosted pools are slow to add nodes.

Quick details:
- Affected route: POST /v1/generate (model: redwood-v2-large)
- Errors: 5xx (502/504) and 429 bursts (concurrent request throttling)
- Time window: ~07:45–now (08:05)
- We've attached an error dump and a screenshot of the 429 dashboard.

This is impacting live clinical inference for our triage engine. Can you escalate to infra and ops immediately? We need an ETA and any mitigation steps.

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 08:25 AM neha_kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks for the heads up, Amit — looping in infra. Marcus / Vivek / Monica: can you triage now?

Quick update from the runtime side. Initial findings (first-pass):
- We're seeing sustained 100% GPU utilization on several nodes serving AstraMed's Dedicated/Hosted mixed pool.
- Autoscaler logs show provisioning requests queued and backoff retries from our cloud provider (GCP) between 07:47–08:15 — there was a short quota/error window causing delayed instance creation.
- Client-side retries from AstraMed are amplifying the load; their workers retry at T+0/T+1 without exponential backoff (we're seeing request bursts).
- KV/prefix cache hit rates dropped ~40% during the spike (likely due to many new warm requests after a burst), increasing per-token compute cost.

Immediate mitigation options (we can perform in parallel):
1) Emergency scale-up: manually add +4 warm nodes to AstraMed's dedicated pool (requires infra approval) — will buy ~6–10 minutes to provision.
2) Apply a temporary per-route concurrency cap (shed excess traffic at the gateway) to prevent GPU saturation and reduce 5xxs/504s.
3) Turn on model fallback to redwood-v2-small-quant (lower latency/cost, smaller memory footprint) for non-critical routes to free capacity.
4) Apply ingress request throttling with stricter retry-after headers to clients (inform AstraMed to slow down retries).

I'll start step 2 & 4 immediately (config change) and prepare an autoscaler manual scale request. Need infra/run approvals for step 1.

Attaching autoscale metrics snapshot.

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 08:40 AM marcus_lin@redwood.ai wrote:
> Quick update from the runtime side. Initial findings (first-pass): ...

Thanks — I see the same in the control plane. Root cause appears to be twofold: (1) GCP transient quota/agent failures caused provisioning latency, and (2) unbounded client-side retries created a feedback loop that exhausted available warmed slots.

Actions taken (09:00–09:12):
- Manually increased the dedicated pool by +3 warm GPUs for AstraMed (request accepted by cloud partner). Provisioning ETA ~7 mins.
- Applied temporary per-route concurrency cap = 120 concurrent requests to reduce queueing on each node.
- Inserted Retry-After: 10s on 429 responses and set gateway to return 503 (soft-fail) for surplus requests to avoid long-tail 504s.
- Kicked off a job to pre-warm 6 extra KV cache shards for AstraMed to restore hit-rate.

Expected customer-visible impact: error rates should drop within ~10–12 mins as new nodes come online and retries back off. We'll monitor.

I'll keep the execs looped. Vivek

—Vivek Kulkarni

Subject: Incident summary & next steps — AstraMed 5xx/429 spike (Nov 3)

Summary:
- Incident window: 07:45–09:40 PST (customer-visible errors), residual elevated latency until ~10:30 PST.
- Root cause (prelim): transient cloud provisioning/quota errors slowed autoscaler, which under heavy client retries led to GPU pool exhaustion and a retry storm. Cache warmups were also disrupted, reducing efficiency.

Actions taken:
- Emergency scale-up (+3 warm GPUs then +2 further) and KV shard pre-warm; per-route concurrency caps and retry-after headers applied; model fallbacks considered but not globally applied to avoid correctness regressions.
- Customer-facing: temporary request caps rolled, ongoing monitoring, and a 48-hour postmortem commitment.

Open items / owners:
- Marcus: full runtime logs, autoscaler traces, and cache metrics (deliver EOD).
- Vivek: work with cloud partner to understand provisioning failure and add provider-side retries/fallbacks (deliver 48–72h remediation plan).
- Monica/Legal: draft credit proposal and customer comms (by EOD).
- Neha/Lauren: coordinate PM/Customer call and postmortem session.

Follow-up: We'll schedule a joint postmortem with AstraMed tomorrow morning. I will personally oversee remediation prioritization.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Success & Escalations
